items.original: The many‑gods objection and the criticisms by Antony Duff and Alan Hájek are central challenges to Pascal’s wager.
items.reworded: The idea that many different deities might exist, together with two prominent criticisms, forms the main obstacle to the classic argument that it is rational to believe because of the possible infinite reward.

items.original: Pascal’s wager seems to make it rational to hold mutually exclusive beliefs, thereby establishing nothing at all.
items.reworded: The old bet about belief seems to let a person rationally accept contradictory positions, so it ultimately establishes nothing.

items.original: The book fails to engage with the philosophy of time, leaving the question ‘what is time?’ unanswered.

e1.limits: The query is a reworded version of a claim the Extractor took from the source paper's abstract, and that claim is itself in the claims index, so this measures recovery of a known move under paraphrase, not discovery of unknown prior art. Items come from the whole corpus of the topic (Decision theory in philosophy of religion: its searches plus recent work in the area), not only from papers directly on it. Corpus: OpenAlex abstracts only (no PhilArchive). One rewording per item; no human labels. Recall is scored per work: OpenAlex lists many papers more than once (versions), so duplicate records are merged (title + first-author surname) before taking the top 5; recall_at_5_strict_record gives the stricter record-level score.
